title: Review of Public Agencies Exemption Provisions in Personal Data Protection Act
what_it_is: Review of Public Agencies Exemption Provisions in Personal Data Protection Act

sections.label: Public Sector Governance Act safeguards
sections.summary: The 2018 Public Sector (Governance) Act added safeguards for public sector personal data, including criminalising misuse by public servants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In 2018, the Public Sector (Governance) Act (PSGA) was introduced and it provided for additional safeguards for personal data in the public sector, including criminalising the misuse of data by public servants.

sections.label: Audits and data protection standards
sections.summary: These laws impose high responsibility on public agencies, with extra requirements for sensitive data and regular mandatory audits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Collectively, these laws impose a high standard of responsibility on all public agencies, with additional requirements for the protection of sensitive or confidential data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Also, regular mandatory audits are conducted to ensure that public agencies comply with the standards for data protection and the security of information and communications technology systems.

sections.label: Different public and private sector approaches
sections.summary: Different approaches are adopted for public and private sectors, so the PDPA applies only to the private sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Because of these important differences, we need and have adopted different approaches to the protection of personal data in the public and in the private sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: That is also why the PDPA applies only to the private sector, while the PSGA and other legislation govern data protection in the public sector.

sections.label: SingHealth and PDPC role
sections.summary: The Member asks whether the Minister agrees SingHealth falls under the PDPA, not as a Public Agency, and the PDPC can play a useful role.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does the Minister agree, because SingHealth is a body that comes within the purview of PDPA, it is not a Public Agency as defined in the Act, and the SingHealth cyberattack case has shown that the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) can actually play a very useful role as far as the public is concerned?

sections.label: Public sector exemption not lower standard
sections.summary: Saying the public sector is exempt from the PDPA does not mean it is subject to a different or lower data security standard.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: When we say exempt – and that is the language that the Member has used in her question – that the public sector is exempt from the PDPA, that does not mean that the public sector is somehow subject to a different or lower standard, as might be implied, in terms of data security and safety.

sections.label: Same or higher public sector standards
sections.summary: The public sector is subject to the same, if not higher, standards because entrusted data is expected to be dealt with securely.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: In fact, we subject the public sector to the same kind of standards, if not higher standards, precisely because we know that the data that is being entrusted to the public sector is done with the confidence that it would be dealt with in a secure manner.

sections.label: SingHealth COI recommendations
sections.summary: The Member said PDPC made useful recommendations, but the key recommendations came from the Government-established Committee of Inquiry.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: On the SingHealth piece, the Member made the point that PDPC came out with the recommendations and so on which were very useful and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: But actually, if you look at the morphology of the entire incident, the key recommendations that came out of this was actually from the Committee of Inquiry (COI) which the Government established.

sections.label: Police reports and public sector standards
sections.summary: A Police report can be made if a crime is thought committed, and the public sector faces the same or higher data governance standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And you can also, if you think a crime has been committed, make a Police report, and that will also be investigated.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, if I can summarise, we subject our public sector to the same, if not higher, rigorous standards of data governance.

sections.label: PDPC handling public sector complaints
sections.summary: PDPC receives some public sector complaints, does not turn them away, and refers matters outside the PDPA to the Government agencies involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: By the way, the PDPC does receive complaints sometimes pertaining to the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, as a recipient of such complaints from the public, it does not turn them away.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Rather, the standing arrangement is that they look at it and, if the jurisdiction is such that it does not come under the PDPA, they then refer it to the Government agencies involved to then follow through.

sections.label: Recourse mechanisms and public sector standards
sections.summary: Members should have no doubt that appropriate recourse mechanisms exist and that public sector data governance standards are not inferior to private sector standards.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, there should be no doubt in Members' minds that we have the appropriate recourse mechanisms.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: There should also be no doubt in Members' minds that the public sector's data governance standards are in no way inferior to the standards that we impose on the private sector.
